Method

Ladder Meta's Ad Library by start date, oldest cutoff first. Whatever survives is that brand's longest runner — provably, not sampled.

Dedupe on CDN content id, then cluster by concept, so each brand's cards are different arguments.

The index

Every ad carries a job (the moment, 18 values) and its mechanisms (the belief levers, 14 values). Both hand-assigned, both closed lists.

Filter by them to cut across brands: every blame-relocation ad, every unsayable symptom, every ad working a named hour of the day.

Days running is not performance

The Ad Library exposes no spend and no impressions for US commercial ads. This measures how long a team kept paying — conviction, not return.

Cadence differs 25× here. Compare within a brand, never across the table.

No volume figures

The scan stops once it has the long runners; 102 of 120 brands stopped early. Any creative count would measure the scrape, not the advertiser.

544 hand-read, 327 auto-tagged, 115 unread.

What repeats

Hormones are the villain. Both sexes.

Cortisol, testosterone, peri-menopause. Same job in six brands: move the cause of a body you dislike from your behaviour to your biology. Happy Mammoth, Primal Queen and Mars Men are one psychographic in three costumes. It isn't my fault, and the mechanism has a name.

GLP-1 makes personas, not demand.

The patient whose appetite vanished. The one with constipation. The man refusing injections. Huel, Grüns, Primal Queen and Mars Men each serve one of them. Three buyers, one drug. Treat it as a single audience and you leave two unserved.

Doctors nobody employs.

Lab coats at Primal Queen and Resilia. Doctor reacts at Ulike. A real cancer researcher. Yale-educated scientists. Not one of them works for the advertiser. The buyer distrusts their own doctor and trusts a credentialed dissenter.

Sorry is an offer.

We made too much. We really fcked up this time. Apologies to last week's buyers. Frame the discount as a mistake and the price drops without the product being worth less.

Premium stopped discounting.

RŌZ's longest runner is a checkout screen reading Due Today $0.00. Norse Organics makes its returns policy the efficacy claim: acne will never return. Where price is the objection, don't pay yet beats pay less.
